subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Learning Club 1 – Lesson 1: Language booster – Places and directions
outcomes: I can name places in a town like airport, bridge and fire station.
I can follow directions on a map.
I can ask for and give directions in town.

tf.s: Firefighters work at a fire station.
tf.why: A fire station is where firefighters work.

tf.s: Teenagers and adults study at a college.
tf.why: A college is a place to study after school.

tf.s: A bridge is a place where planes land.
tf.why: Planes land at an airport; you go over a bridge.

tf.s: In text 1, the person starts at the airport.
tf.why: The route begins at the airport.

tf.s: On the way to the college, he walks past the fire station.
Adam is trying to go to the stadium.
tf.why: He asks for directions to the stadium.

tf.s: Adam is meeting Faris at the big gate.
tf.why: They meet at the big gate of the stadium.

tf.s: We say “Go over the river” when we walk next to the river.
tf.why: We say go along the river; we go over a bridge.

tf.s: On the map, the red pin shows where you start.
tf.why: The green pin is the start; the red pin is the destination.

tf.s: “Go through the gate” means walk past the gate without going in.
tf.why: Through means you go in one side and out the other.

boxes.why: Firefighters work at a fire station.

boxes.q: You can drive or walk over this. What is it?
boxes.why: A bridge goes over a river or road.

boxes.q: Complete: Go ___ the bridge and then turn left.
Complete: Go ___ the road and go over the bridge.
boxes.why: We cross a road: go across.

boxes.q: Complete: Walk ___ the river, then take the second right.
Complete: Go ___ the big gate and turn left.
Where is Adam trying to go?
boxes.why: Adam wants to go to the stadium.

boxes.q: What does he walk past on the way to the college?
boxes.why: In text 1, he walks past the hospital.

boxes.q: Where do planes land and take off?
On the map, what does the green pin show?
boxes.why: Green is the start; red is the destination.

mcq.q: Which group shows the new town places?
mcq.why: These are the Learning Club places.

mcq.q: Which question asks for directions politely?
o: Excuse me. Can you tell me where the college is, please?

mcq.q: Where does the person start in text 1?
Which is a direction, not a place?
mcq.why: Take the second left tells you where to go.

mcq.q: There is a river between you and the college. What direction fits?
mcq.why: A bridge takes you over the river.

mcq.q: You want to get from one side of the road to the other. What do you do?
mcq.why: Across means from one side to the other.

o: Turn left, go past the hospital and go straight on.
Turn left, go past at the hospital straight.
Go past on the left of straight.
mcq.why: This uses the directions language correctly.

mcq.q: What is the difference between “go along the river” and “go over the river”?
o: Along means next to it; over means you cross it.
Over means you swim in it.
mcq.why: Along follows the river; over crosses it.

mcq.q: Why do maps in the lesson have a green pin and a red pin?
o: To show where you start and where you finish
To show old and new places
To show the shops that are closed
mcq.why: Green is the start; red is the destination.

mcq.q: Which place is the odd one out?
mcq.why: You go over a bridge; the others are buildings.
